items.title: Sony’s 1000XM4C headphones are a Black Friday bargain at $198
items.summary:
The fan-favorite folding design returns with the comfortable, slightly improved XM4C headphones. | Photo: John Higgins / The Verge	

Instead of purely looking forward with its headphone designs, Sony went back to its popular WH-1000XM4 design and made some improvements to make it even better. The 2026 version, called the WH-1000XM4C, sounds nearly as good as the pricier XM6 model (currently $348), but is down to $198 during Black Friday at Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart. That’s $100 off their October launch price.
Sony WH-1000XM4C

Where to Buy:

 $299.99 $198 at Amazon
 $299.99 $198 at Walmart
 $299.99 $199.99 at Best Buy

There’s a reason why Sony went back to refine the XM4. Our former reviewer Chris Welch praised them for being super comfortable and for having close to perfect features for the price, especially compared to its successor, the XM3 (still my daily driver, for what it’s worth). The XM4s had better sound quality and noise cancellation, plus improved mics, multipoint connectivity, and a sensor that can detect when you remove them to automatically pause audio. Now, with the XM4C, there are further improvements, most notably a 10-band equalizer in the app (compared to the original XM4’s five-band) that my colleague John Higgins says really helped the headphones’ midrange frequencies open up.
These are a great buy, but they aren’t your only Sony headphones deal to consider right now. Sony’s WH-1000XM5 are available during Black Friday at Best Buy for $169, their lowest price yet from a major retailer. There are upsides and downsides to this model: They feature improved noise cancellation thanks to more mics, despite using the same ANC chip as the XM4C, but they can’t fold up as compactly, making them a little bigger to pack in your bag. Either one you choose, you’ll have some great headphones to listen to going into 2027.
Read our Sony WH-1000XM4C review.

items.title: This purple electric Chinese minivan can go up to 559 miles on a charge
items.summary:
Electric minivans could be the ultimate in utility, with room for passengers, gear, and huge batteries. While VW's ID Buzz only gave us 200 miles of real-world driving on a charge in 2023, China's BYD has just announced a flagship purple peoplemover that can go an estimated 559 miles (900 km) on electricity.
It's called the BYD Whale, and some back-of-the-napkin math suggests it lives up to the name. The van would be bigger than a Honda Odyssey, bigger than a Chrysler Pacifica, and bigger than a Toyota Sienna, at 17.3 feet (5,270mm) long, 6.5 feet (1,996mm) wide, 6 feet (1,815mm) tall, and with a 123-inch (3,130mm) wheelbase.

items.title: The best Black Friday deals you can still get on AirPods, Macs, and other Apple gear
items.summary:
The MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR has hit a new low price just a few months after release. | Photo: Antonio G. Di Benedetto / The Verge	

Black Friday is entering the evening, which means one of the best times of the year to save some cash on a new pair of AirPods or the latest Apple Watch is coming to a close. After all, the holiday savings can help offset the unfortunate price hikes from earlier this year, when Apple raised the cost of some of its most popular gear. Some discounts still apply to recent releases like the Apple Watch Series 12 and touchscreen MacBook Pro, too, which are available at their lowest prices to date.
In addition to a variety of discounts across retailers, Apple is offering up to $300 in gift cards with select purchases between November 27th and November 30th. How much you get back is determined by how much you spend, with up to $100 available for some iPhone and Apple Watch purchases, and up to $300 for the 16-inch MacBook Pro. That said, in some cases you may be able to save more by buying from other retailers.
Earbud and headphone deals
AirPods Pro 3
The latest AirPods Pro offer improved noise cancellation and richer bass, along with built-in heart sensors that work with Apple’s Fitness app to monitor calories burned across more than 50 workouts. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

 $249 $149 at Amazon
 $249 $149 at Walmart
 $249 $149.99 at Best Buy


Beats Powerbeats Pro 2
Beats’ fitness-focused earbuds feature ear hooks designed to stay put during even the most intense workouts as well as built-in heart rate monitoring. They also deliver relatively bass-rich sound for their design, along with solid noise cancellation, wireless charging, and AirPods features like adaptive audio thanks to Apple’s H2 chip. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

 $249 $179.95 at Amazon
 $249 $179.95 at Walmart
 $249.99 $179.99 at Best Buy

You can buy the AirPods 4 on sale at Walmart for around $89 ($40 off), which is $20 shy of their best price. Apple’s last-gen earbuds lack active noise cancellation, but they still deliver good, relatively bass-rich sound, even if they don’t quite match the newer AirPods 5. They also offer voice call quality on par with the latest AirPods Pro. Read our review.
The second-gen AirPods Max are down to $419 ($130 off) at Amazon and Best Buy, which is $19 shy of their best price to date (Target also has them for about $10 more). Like the original, Apple’s latest over-ear headphones feature a luxurious build consisting of aluminum, steel, and a mesh fabric, but they offer better sound and noise cancellation. The new H2 chip also enables features like adaptive audio and live translation. Read our review.
Beats Studio Pro
The latest Beats Studio Pro feature improved noise cancellation, sound quality, and comfort. They also support lossless audio over USB-C and offer native support for a range of iOS and Android features like other Beats headphones. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

 $349.99 $139.95 at Amazon (select colors)
 $349.99 $99 at Walmart (select colors)
 $349.99 $139.95 at Best Buy (select colors)


Beats 360 headphones
The Beats 360 are ANC headphones for people who prefer headphones over earbuds at the gym. They’re Beats’ first IP-rated cans, with ear cushions that you can easily remove for cleaning (or style points). They also stay in place during most exercises, while still delivering solid bass. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

 $349.99 $249 at Amazon
 $349.99 $249.99 at Best Buy

If you want over-ears and are comfortable going without active noise cancellation, the Beats Solo 4 are on sale starting at $79.99 ($120 off) at Amazon and Target — a new low price. The headphones are a noticeable improvement over their predecessor, delivering more detailed sound and support for lossless audio. They also last up to 50 hours on a single charge, while their memory foam ear cushions make them comfortable enough for long listening sessions. Read our review.
The Beats Studio Buds Plus are down to around $89.95 ($80 off) at Amazon, Best Buy, and Target, nearly matching their lowest price to date. The wireless earbuds feature a slick, eye-catching transparent option and solid noise cancellation, especially at this price. They’re also exceptionally comfortable, with four ear tip sizes to help you find a secure fit. Sure, you don’t get wireless charging, but they offer IPX4 water resistance and up to nine hours of battery life on a single charge. Read our review.
MacBook deals 
MacBook Neo
Apple’s most affordable laptop uses the same A18 Pro chip found in the iPhone 16 Pro. It features a vibrant 13-inch display, surprisingly good speakers, and 8GB of RAM, making it a solid option for students and anyone who needs a laptop for everyday tasks. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

 $799 $699.99 at Amazon (512GB, Touch ID)
 $699 $649 at Best Buy (256GB)
 $699 $599 at Amazon (256GB)


Apple MacBook Air (M5)
Apple’s latest MacBook Air features an M5 chip and starts with 512GB of storage, with significantly faster performance than prior generations. It’s still an excellent machine despite the higher base price, especially given the battery life and speakers. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

 $1299 $999 at Amazon (13-inch, 512GB)
 $1299 $999 at Best Buy (13-inch)
 $1499 $1199 at Amazon (15-inch, 512GB)

The recently released 16.3-inch MacBook Pro with a PROLED XDR display, 24GB of RAM, and 1TB of storage is on sale starting at $3,099 ($300 off) — a new low price — at Amazon. The redesigned laptop is Apple’s first with an OLED touchscreen, which allows for rich colors and deep blacks. It’s also noticeably thinner and lighter than the non-touchscreen 16-inch MacBook Pro, and features a new Dynamic Island that replaces the notch and provides quick access to controls and notifications. Read our review.
The 14-inch M6-powered MacBook Pro is on sale starting at $1,749 ($250 off) at Amazon and Best Buy, which is a new low price. The Pro builds on its predecessor with a faster chip and support for Wi-Fi 7. In our testing, it handled multitasking, photo editing, and occasional video editing with ease while still delivering exceptional battery life. It lacks the newer MacBook Pro’s gorgeous OLED display, but its Mini LED screen still looks great, especially given its smooth 120Hz refresh rate. It also offers excellent speakers and a good selection of ports, including three Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI, and an SD card slot. Read our review.
Apple Watch deals
Apple Watch Series 12
The Apple Watch Series 12 introduces AI-powered Audio Intelligence features, including sound recognition alerts, Live Rewind, and Siri Recap. It can also track your heart rate every five seconds, even when you’re not exercising, and offers faster charging than prior models. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

 $399 $299 at Amazon (GPS, 42mm)
 $399 $329 at Best Buy (GPS, 42mm)
 $449 $349 at Amazon (GPS, 46mm)

The Apple Watch SE 3 is on sale in the 40mm / GPS configuration starting at $179 ($50 off) at Amazon and Walmart, matching its best price to date, while Best Buy is currently $20 higher. Apple’s newest entry-level smartwatch remains our top recommendation for anyone who wants a basic fitness tracker, as it offers all the essentials alongside an always-on display and Apple’s S10 chip, which enables on-device Siri requests. Read our review.
AirTags, chargers, and other deals
Apple AirTag (second-gen)
Apple’s latest AirTags feature an upgraded ultra-wideband chip for more precise location tracking, a noticeably louder speaker, and an expanded Bluetooth range. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

 $29 $18 at Amazon
 $29 $18 at Walmart
 $29 $18 at Best Buy


Baseus AM52 power bank (with built-in cable)
The Baseus PicoGo AM52 is a 10,000mAh magnetic power bank that supports fast 25W Qi2.2 wireless charging and up to 45W wired charging via its built-in USB-C cable. It was one of the fastest wireless chargers we tested, bringing an iPhone 17 Pro Max to 65 percent in an hour. Read our guide to the best Qi2 batteries.

Where to Buy:

 $79.99 $51.99 at Amazon (orange)
 $79.99 $56.98 at Amazon (black)
 $79.99 $59.99 at Amazon (pink)


Apple iPad (11th-gen)
Apple’s 11th-gen iPad offers 128GB of storage — twice that of its predecessor — and runs on a faster A16 chip. It also comes in four colors: blue, pink, yellow, and silver.

Where to Buy:

 $449 $379 at Amazon (128GB, Wi-Fi)
 $449 $379 at Walmart (128GB, Wi-Fi)

You can buy the last-gen iPad Mini with 128GB of storage and Wi-Fi on Amazon in select colors for $484 ($115 off), which is the best price we’ve seen since Apple’s recent price hikes. It has a smaller screen and a slower chip than the newer model, and it lacks an OLED screen, the Acoustic Display, and water resistance. Still, it’s a great option for reading and everyday use that’s currently more affordable than its $599 successor, with support for Apple Intelligence and the Apple Pencil Pro. Read our review.
Apple’s latest Magic Mouse is matching its all-time low of $59.99 ($20 off) at Amazon. The wireless mouse features a touch-sensitive surface that lets you scroll through documents and swipe between apps with simple gestures; it also pairs automatically with compatible Macs and offers support for USB-C.
Apple Pencil (USB-C)
Apple’s entry-level stylus attaches magnetically to supported iPads, though it doesn’t support magnetic charging. Instead, you pair and charge it by connecting it to your device’s USB-C port. It includes tilt sensitivity and Apple Pencil Hover support, but it doesn’t offer double-tap gestures or pressure sensitivity.

 $79 $49 at Best Buy

The Icemag 3 can wirelessly deliver up to 25W of power to compatible smartphones and up to 35W wired charging via USB-C. The 10,000mAh Qi2 charger can also act as a foldable kickstand, comes with an integrated USB-C cable that serves as a lanyard, and sports a transparent design with colorful RGB lighting.

Apple Studio Display (2026)
Designed to pair with a Mac, the latest Apple Studio Display features a sharp 5K Retina display, a great 12-megapixel Center Stage camera that keeps you in frame during video calls, and a good six-speaker sound system with spatial audio. Sadly, it only offers two Thunderbolt 5 ports in addition to a pair of USB-C ports. Read our review.

items.title: The best robot vacuums we’ve tested are up to 60 percent off for Black Friday
items.summary:
The Eufy Omni C28 has dropped to a new low of $379.99 for Black Friday. | Photo: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge	

Black Friday is here, and if you want a little help keeping your floors clean this holiday season, now is a great time to pick up a robot vacuum. Some of the best models we’ve tested over the last year or two are on sale for up to 60 percent off, whether you’re after a basic robovac for quick cleanups or a more advanced model that vacuums, mops, and practically takes care of itself.
This year’s sale has made some pricier robot vacuums a lot more affordable. The Eufy Omni C28, for example, now costs about what you’d expect to pay for a budget bot, while the Matic — which impressed us with its almost humanlike navigation — is getting a rare discount in the form of a bundle. If none of those are quite what you’re looking for, we’ve also found good deals on models from Roborock, Dreame, and more, with picks below for a variety of budgets and cleaning needs.
Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Flow
Roborock’s first roller-mop robot vacuum, the Curv 2 Flow, features flagship specs at a midrange price, including excellent mopping, a retractable mop cover, 20,000Pa suction, AI-powered obstacle avoidance, and a compact design. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

 $999.99 $549.99 at Amazon 
 $999.99 $549.99 at Roborock

Roborock Q10 S5 Plus
Despite lacking a multifunction dock, the budget-friendly robot vacuum and mop offers an impressive set of features for the price, including AI-powered obstacle avoidance, sonic mopping, automatic mop lifting, and a self-emptying dock.

Where to Buy:

 $549.99 $229.99 at Amazon
 $549.99 $229.99 at Roborock

Matic robot vacuum
The Matic robot vacuum and mop is ideal for cluttered homes with pets, multiple floors, and a mixture of carpets and hardwood. It offers almost humanlike navigation, tackling high-pile rugs and mopping up wet spills. The quiet bot also requires less maintenance than many rivals thanks to its onboard water tank and dust bag. Read our review.


Where to Buy:

 $1795 $1395 at Matic (Standard Bundle)
 $1995 $1595 at Matic (Serene Bundle)

Eufy Omni C28
The Eufy Omni C28 combines excellent mopping performance with a small self-cleaning dock that’s well suited for apartments and other smaller spaces. It navigates around furniture and into tight areas with ease, while its roller mop does a great job cleaning hard floors.

Where to Buy:

 $799.99 $379.99 at Amazon
 $799.99 $379.99 at Eufy (with code WS24C28200NEW1)

Dreame X60 Ultra
The Dreame X60 Ultra is a powerful robot vacuum and mop that does a great job of cleaning carpets thanks to its dual roller brushes and 35,000Pa of suction. It can climb over tall thresholds, squeeze under low furniture, and automatically detach its mop pads when vacuuming carpets.

Where to Buy:

 $1499.99 $999.99 at Amazon
 $1499.99 $999.99 at Best Buy (with Dreame W10 vacuum)
 $1499.99 $999.99 at Dreame

Narwal Flow 2
The Narwal Flow 2 is an excellent robot vacuum for hardwood floors. A superb mop with a wide flat roller pad and a good vacuum, the Flow 2 also has top-notch navigation and obstacle detection. Its sleek base station is also less of an eyesore than most models. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

 $1499.99 $899.99 at Amazon (with on-page coupon)
 $1499.99 $949.99 at Wayfair

Roborock Saros 20
Roborock’s Saros 20 stands out for its ability to climb tall thresholds, avoid obstacles with impressive accuracy, and clean under low furniture thanks to its slim design. It also combines powerful 36,000Pa suction with great spinning mop pads, which is why we recommend it for homes with multiple floor types and tricky transitions between rooms.

Where to Buy:

 $1599.99 $989.99 at Amazon
 $1599.99 $989.99 at Walmart
 $1599.99 $989.99 at Roborock

Ecovacs Deebot X12 OmniCyclone
Ecovacs’ robot vacuum and mop can pretreat stains, keep carpets dry with a smart mop cover, and deliver powerful 22,000Pa suction. It also includes an all-in-one dock that automatically empties the dustbin, refills the water tanks, and washes the mop with heated, pressurized water.

Where to Buy:

 $1499.99 $749 at Amazon
 $1499.99 $749 at Best Buy

Switchbot K11 Plus
The Matter-compatible SwitchBot  K11 Plus is ideal for small apartments, bedrooms, and home offices. It can easily navigate around chair and desk legs and into tight spaces that most other bots miss. It also features a commendable 6,000Pa of suction power — which is great for this price point — and works well on both hardwood and carpet.

Where to Buy:

 $399.99 $169.56 at Amazon (with on-page coupon)
 $399.99 $160 at SwitchBot (with code BFCMX60)

Dreame X50 Ultra
With high suction power, an improved brush system, and the ability to scale thresholds up to 6cm, the X50 Ultra stands out as a great robot vacuum-mop hybrid. While its 20,000Pa suction isn’t quite as powerful as the X60 Ultra’s and it can’t tackle especially high thresholds as well, it’s still an excellent option. Its edge cleaning also isn’t quite as effective as the X60 Ultra’s, but you’re otherwise getting many of the same features for a lot less.

Where to Buy:

 $1599.99 $799.99 at Dreame 
 $1599.99 $799.99 at Target

Dreame L40 Ultra Gen 2
The Dreame L40 Ultra Gen 2 delivers powerful 25,000Pa suction, AI-powered obstacle avoidance, and a self-cleaning dock that empties the dustbin, washes the mop, and refills its water tanks. Unlike the X50 Ultra, however, it lacks the ability to climb high thresholds or stairs.

Where to Buy:

 $799.99 $474.98 at Amazon

Narwal Freo X Ultra
The Freo X Ultra features spinning triangular mop pads and can swing slightly to reach baseboards. Its large charging dock holds two big water tanks, while Narwal’s disposable onboard bin compresses the dust. It’s also relatively quiet when it returns to the dock, and its anti-tangle brush and 8,200Pa of suction perform well on most carpets.

Where to Buy:

Blade Runner 2049 looks fantastic, even if you pick up the 1080p Blu-ray version. | Image: Alcon Entertainment	

No shade to those who love their subscription services, but viewing physical movies is a time-honored tradition that shouldn’t go away. Watching them doesn’t feel all that different, but deciding which movie to watch feels less annoying; sifting through a movie collection on your shelf or in a storage binder is so much more fun (and less overwhelming) than scrolling endlessly in apps.
While standard Blu-ray players that display movies at up to 1080p are fairly inexpensive, 4K Blu-ray counterparts that can show movies in all their 4K HDR glory are significantly pricier (but totally worth it if you’re a movie buff). No matter the player you own, there are always Blu-ray deals, and the discounts are especially good during Black Friday. We’ve highlighted some of our favorites below, though Amazon, Barnes & Noble, and Gruv are each overflowing with more deals than we could realistically wedge into our coverage.

items.title: Abelina - Official Demo Launch Trailer
The new iPad Mini is getting its first major discount for Black Friday
items.summary:
I’m not saying you should read on an iPad next to fountain. I’m just saying you can. | Photo: David Pierce / The Verge	

We were big fans of Apple’s new iPad Mini when we reviewed it in early November, but its steep starting price of $699 was hard to swallow. Thankfully, the small tablet is already getting a sizable discount for Black Friday. Right now, Amazon and Walmart are both selling the 2026 iPad Mini with Wi-Fi and 128GB of storage starting at $599 ($100 off), its lowest price to date.
iPad Mini (2026)

Where to Buy:

 $699 $599 at Amazon (Wi-Fi, 128GB)
 $699 $599 at Walmart (Wi-Fi, 128GB) 
 $799 $749 at Amazon (Wi-Fi, 256GB)

The new Mini is a notable upgrade over its predecessor, with a larger 8.5-inch OLED display that delivers deeper blacks and better contrast than the previous model’s 8.3-inch LCD. Despite the bigger screen, the tablet itself is smaller and lighter, making it easier to carry. Apple also added IP67 dust and water resistance, so you have less reason to worry about where you use it. As my colleague David Pierce noted in his review, that made a big difference in his day-to-day use; he felt more comfortable handing the Mini to his spill-prone toddler or keeping it nearby in the kitchen to follow recipes. He even took it into the shower to keep watching a football game.
The upgraded A20 Pro chip also made apps load faster and demanding games run better in Pierce’s testing, while battery life held steady at around nine hours of screentime. At $599, though, the new Mini is still relatively expensive if you mainly want a tablet for browsing the web or streaming shows. The last-gen iPad Mini, which runs on Apple’s A17 Pro chip, is available for under $500 if you’d rather save another $100 and can live without the OLED screen and water resistance. But if you’ve been waiting for a more worthwhile upgrade to Apple’s smallest tablet, the current Black Friday discount makes the new model easier to justify.
iPad Mini (2024)

Where to Buy:

 $599 $484 at Amazon (128GB, Wi-Fi)
 $699 $584 at Amazon (256GB, Wi-Fi)

items.title: The 25 best gaming deals we’ve found so far for Black Friday
items.summary:
A discounted one-year subscription to World of Warcraft is among the Black Friday deals. | Image: Blizzard	

While deals on consoles and key PC components are in short supply during Black Friday (or simply not good enough to warrant covering), there are numerous fantastic discounts on video games, accessories, and monitors to make up for it. We thought it’d be useful to display all of the deals we think are worth your attention on one page instead of sprinkled here and there in our coverage.
Below, you’ll find the very best discounts we’ve found for PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC players to shop. You can filter the table below to display exactly the type of products you’re looking for. 
Sony DualSense Edge
Both the white and midnight black versions of the DualSense Edge are discounted. Refurbished versions (with the same warranty as new controllers) are another $25 off.

Where to Buy:

 $199 $169 at Amazon
 $199 $169.99 at Best Buy
 $169 $144 at PlayStation Direct (refurbished)

Nintendo Switch 2 + Mario Kart World Bundle
The Nintendo Switch 2 features a 7.9-inch LCD display, magnetically attached Joy-Con 2 controllers, backward compatibility with most original Switch games, and exclusive titles like Donkey Kong Bananza and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

 $549.99 $499 at Amazon
 $549.99 $499 at Walmart
 $549.99 $499.99 at Best Buy

Samsung P9 microSD Express card
The P9 is great if you need more storage for your Nintendo Switch 2. The microSD Express card offers sequential read speeds of up to 800MB/s, but only gadgets with a microSD Express card slot can take full advantage of the highest speeds. That includes certain cameras, tablets, and drones with a microSD USH-I slot.

Where to Buy:

 $79.99 $44.99 at Amazon (256GB)
 $149.99 $92.99 at Amazon (512GB)

Donkey Kong Bananza
Donkey Kong Bananza is one of the Switch 2’s first exclusive must-have titles. Its destructible environment allows you to smash your way through each of its 17 levels, and the paths you make will remain intact unless you specifically choose to reset the world. Your companion Pauline’s singing allows you to transform into animals that have abilities that allow you to reach previously inaccessible parts of levels. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

 $69.99 $49.99 at Best Buy (Physical)
 $69.99 $49.99 at Target (Physical)
 $69.99 $49.99 at Amazon (Digital)

8BitDo Pro 3 Wireless Controller
The Pro 3 features swappable ABXY face buttons and joystick caps, providing players with a highly customizable experience. It also features new L4 and R4 macro buttons between the triggers and its USB-C charging port, along with more durable and power efficient TMR joysticks.

Where to Buy:

 $69.99 $54.99 at Amazon (purple)
 $69.99 $47.39 at Amazon (gray)

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
Nintendo’s latest Switch 2 exclusive is the best way to relive what is arguably the best Zelda game of all time. The revamped visuals look gorgeous, and while the game’s improved controls might annoy some purists who still cling to the heyday of ’98, we reckon most folks won’t bat an eye.

Where to Buy:

 $59.99 $54.99 at Amazon (Digital)
 $69 $62.99 at Costco (Physical)

Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition
The Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition includes both the base game and the “Shadow of the Erdtree” expansion, along with new customization options.

Where to Buy:

 $79.99 $59.88 at Amazon (Switch 2, physical)

Fractal Scape gaming headset
The Fractal Scape gaming headset has a sleek, refined design, with a 2.4GHz low-latency connection and excellent sound for gaming or music.

Where to Buy:

 $199.99 $159.99 at Amazon (gray)
 $199.99 $159.99 at Amazon (black)
 $199.99 $159.99 at B&H Photo

Meta Quest 3S
The Meta Quest 3S is a battery-powered standalone VR headset that has the same chipset as the pricier Quest 3, but with the same lenses and screen resolution as the Quest 2. In addition to being able to play many games from the Meta Store, it can also be connected to a gaming PC to play VR games like Half-Life Alyx. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

 $349 $297 at Amazon (128GB)
 $349 $297 at Walmart (128GB)
 $349 $297.49 at Best Buy (128GB)

Nex Playground
The Nex Playground is a motion-controlled console that connects to your TV and uses a built-in camera and AI to track your movements as you play. Designed for ages five and up, it comes with games like Fruit Ninja and Whac-a-Mole. You can download more games, including titles featuring popular characters like Elmo, with a paid Play Pass subscription.

Where to Buy:

 $299 $209 at Amazon
 $299 $209 at Walmart
 $299 $209 at Best Buy

World of Warcraft Celebration Pass
The World of Warcraft Celebration Pass cuts the price of a 12-month subscription during Black Friday, offering access to World of Modern WoW, WoW: Forever, and WoW: Classic at a discounted rate.

Where to Buy:

 $155.88 $120 at Battle.net

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered
The Witcher 3 lets you explore the war-torn Northern Kingdoms as Geralt of Rivia while preparing to face the mysterious Wild Hunt. The recent remaster adds improved visuals, smoother combat, and better movement, cementing the game’s status as one of the best RPGs of all time.

Where to Buy:

 $49.99 $19.99 at PlayStation Store (PS5)

Logitech G Pro X2 Superstrike
Clicking the Superstrike feels like using a regular gaming mouse, which is impressive considering there are no mechanical switches inside. Instead, it uses haptics to emulate the effect (to great effect).

Where to Buy:

 $179.99 $149.99 at Amazon
 $179.99 $149.99 at Best Buy
 $179.99 $107.99 at eBay (w/ code CYBERFINDS20)

Alienware 32-inch 4K OLED gaming monitor
One of the most affordable Tandem RGB Stripe OLEDs is even cheaper during Black Friday. The AW3226Q monitor has a 165Hz refresh rate, G-Sync compatibility, better-looking text rendering than most other OLED monitors, and unbeatable contrast.

Where to Buy:

 $699.99 $549.99 at Dell

LG B6E OLED TV
Make this the year that the gamer in your life has an OLED TV to play their console games on. Despite being affordable, the B6E doesn’t skimp on features.

Where to Buy:

 $1399.99 $699.99 at Best Buy (55-inch)
 $1899.99 $999.99 at Best Buy (65-inch)
 $2699.99 $1499.99 at Best Buy (77-inch)

Design Room subscription
A gift for the gamer who already has all the gear they need (and who loves to read about gaming when they’re not gaming). The site focuses on well-researched deep dives and oral histories on classic video games.

Where to Buy:

 $7 at Design Room

Sony PlayStation 27-inch 1440p gaming monitor
The 1440p 240Hz refresh rate screen is sleek, but pretty basic for the price. It stands out, though, thanks to its DualSense-charging cradle that extends from its bottom. This is the first discount.

Where to Buy:

 $349.99 $299.99 at Best Buy
 $349.99 $299.99 at PlayStation Direct

Sony PlayStation DualSense controller – Chroma series
If you’re seeking out a prettier DualSense, the Chroma series of controllers are just a few bucks more than the standard color schemes.

Where to Buy:

 $79.99 $59.99 at Amazon
 $79.99 $59.99 at Walmart

Star Wars Galactic Racer
No game has delivered more thrills per minute (TPM) this year than Star Wars Galactic Racer. Podracing is back, and it’s better than ever with this title’s stellar sense of speed, plus it has a surprisingly memorable cast of characters.

Where to Buy:

 $59.99 $30 at Amazon (PS5)
 $59.99 $49.99 at Amazon (Xbox)

Nintendo eShop gift cards
Everyone knows gift cards aren’t the best gift, but with such steep discounts happening on Nintendo eShop credit, you can save a lot on a Switch 2, or games and accessories, if you’re alright with jumping through a couple extra hoops.

Where to Buy:

 $200 $168 at Newegg ($200, w/ code BFF3532)
 $200 $159.99 at Costco ($200)

Halo: Campaign Evolved
Halo: Campaign Evolved lets you revisit the original Halo: Combat Evolved campaign with better graphics, updated controls, and improved sound. The well-crafted remake also adds three new missions starring Master Chief and Sgt. Johnson, which take place before the main campaign. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

 $49.99 $29.99 at PlayStation Store (PS5)
 $49.99 $29.99 at Steam (PC)

Xreal One Pro AR glasses
USB-C display glasses can make travel (or relaxing on the couch) more fun by putting a huge virtual screen in front of your face. Xreal’s One Pro are some of the best out there at displaying content from your phone, tablet, laptop, or portable handheld.

Where to Buy:

 $649 $499 at Amazon
 $649 $524.99 at Best Buy
 $649 $499 at Xreal Shop

Pokémon Pokopia
Nintendo’s latest Pokémon spinoff for the Switch 2 is part Pokémon, part Minecraft, and part Animal Crossing. Yet, despite borrowing gameplay mechanics from each, the cozy life sim is more than the sum of its expansive, building-centric parts. It’s breezy and warm-hearted, with enough secrets to keep you occupied for hours on end.

Where to Buy:

 $69.99 $62.99 at Amazon (Digital)

Elgato Stream Deck MK. 2
The MK.2 version of the standard Stream Deck comes with 15 programmable buttons, a swappable faceplate, and a detachable stand.

Where to Buy:

 $149.99 $109.99 at Amazon
 $149.99 $109.99 at Best Buy 
 $149.99 $109.99 at B&H Photo

Resident Evil Requiem
The latest entry in the long-running survival horror series returned in 2026, with two different styles of gameplay (tense first-person and guns-blazing third-person perspectives) via its dual protagonists. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

 $69.99 $39.99 at Amazon (PS5)
 $69.99 $39.99 at Best Buy (PS5)
